title: Choose the Gate Trial screen
question: The trial keeps the Forest Light design. Which arrangement should guide its preparation and phase screens?

options.label: The threshold
options.thesis: A quiet arrival screen gives the Gate Trial room, then brings readiness and the five phases into view.
options.viewport: The forest fills the upper half with the trial name; readiness and the first phase sit on paper below.
options.risk: The large arrival band gives less room to the checklist on a small phone.

options.label: The daybook
options.thesis: A single working page keeps the whole trial visible like a dated field record.
options.viewport: A compact header gives way to a readiness strip and all five phases in a continuous ledger.
options.risk: Its steady density feels less ceremonial when the trial begins.

options.label: One station at a time
options.thesis: The active phase takes the screen, with a small route showing the work around it.
options.viewport: The walk phase opens first with a clear place for its result; the remaining phases stay visible as route stops.
options.risk: The person must move between phases to see the full trial at once.
